result.question: How has Nvidia's data center business contributed to its revenue growth across its last three fiscal years?
result.answer:
NVIDIA's data center business has been the primary engine of the company's revenue growth over its last three fiscal years, during which total revenue rose from $60,922 million in fiscal year 2024 (ended January 28, 2024) [xbrl:0001045810-26-000021:us-gaap:Revenues:2024-01-28] to $130,497 million in fiscal year 2025 (ended January 26, 2025) [xbrl:0001045810-26-000021:us-gaap:Revenues:2025-01-26] and then to $215,938 million in fiscal year 2026 (ended January 25, 2026) [xbrl:0001045810-26-000021:us-gaap:Revenues:2026-01-25].

Data Center revenue grew from $47,525 million in fiscal year 2024 to $115,186 million in fiscal year 2025 and to $193,737 million in fiscal year 2026 [0001045810-26-000021:item-15-p037]. Within Data Center, Compute revenue rose from $38,950 million in fiscal year 2024 to $102,196 million in fiscal year 2025 and $162,361 million in fiscal year 2026, while Networking revenue grew from $8,575 million to $12,990 million and then to $31,376 million over the same periods [0001045810-26-000021:item-15-p037]. Because total revenue grew by $69,575 million in fiscal year 2025 and $85,441 million in fiscal year 2026 [0001045810-26-000021:item-7-p008], while Data Center revenue grew by $67,661 million and $78,551 million in those years [0001045810-26-000021:item-15-p037], the data center business accounted for the overwhelming majority of the company's revenue growth in each year.

Management's narrative confirms this: demand for data center systems and products surged in fiscal year 2024 [0001045810-24-000029:item-7-p001]; revenue growth in fiscal year 2025 was driven by data center compute and networking platforms for accelerated computing and AI solutions, with demand for the Hopper architecture driving significant full-year growth and Blackwell production systems beginning to ship in the fourth quarter [0001045810-25-000023:item-7-p001]; and revenue growth in fiscal year 2026 was again driven by data center compute and networking platforms for accelerated computing and AI solutions, with the Blackwell architecture representing the majority of Data Center revenue [0001045810-26-000021:item-7-p001]. In fiscal year 2026, revenue from Data Center computing grew 59% driven by demand for the Blackwell computing platform, and revenue from Data Center networking grew 142% driven by the introduction and continued ramp of NVLink compute fabric for GB200 and GB300 systems and the growth of Ethernet and InfiniBand platforms [0001045810-26-000021:item-7-p008].
